rationale.faithfulness: HH339 fails by its own kill rule with pooled power 1.00 in both models; the kickoff control and voluntary erasures behave. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1. The positive alternative (order in work/prompt) is not separated from the agent prior.
rationale.usefulness: A clean operator rule: context resets do not erase room identity (alignment within -7% to +23%), so erasures can be used for loop-breaking without cost to room differentiation. It sharpens the Q4 picture: the context window carries work value, not identity.

one_line: A forced context erasure does not demagnetize an agent's room alignment (delta_F -0.08 [-0.23, 0.07], power 1.00 at a 30% drop): room order lives in the agent's work, prompt and memory, not its context window.

models.note: no context-held room magnetization; alignment does not drop at erasure
natural scramble of the context channel carries ~0 room-order information

v2.claim: A forced context erasure does not drop an agent's alignment with its room's spontaneous axis (δ_F −0.08 [−0.23, 0.07] bge, −0.07 gte over 3,477 erasures; pooled power 1.00 for a 30% drop): room order is not stored in the context window
v2.scope: 8 regime-III two-room periods; natives G38, G51, NE41
v2.decision: erasing context won't reset a room's character; it lives in work, prompt and memory
